title: Banach Contractivity and Decay Profiles of Guarded Language Operators in Weighted First-Disagreement Ultrametric Spaces
content: We study guarded recursive operators on spaces of formal languages equipped with weighted first-disagreement ultrametrics generated by arbitrary decreasing depth profiles. We show that all admissible profiles preserve the same compact complete finite-depth topology while producing substantially different quantitative contraction behavior. A uniform decay profile is introduced to measure the relative decrease of metric weights under guarded disagreement shifts. We determine the exact Lipschitz modulus of canonical guarded contexts and prove that the same decay quantity is the optimal universal Lipschitz coefficient for finite guarded wrapping operators with a prescribed minimal guard length. This leads to an exact universal Banach contractivity criterion and to a sharp guard-length threshold separating uniformly contractive and nonuniform regimes. Independently of Banach contractivity, positive guardedness is shown to guarantee a unique fixed language, global Picard convergence, and explicit finite-depth stabilization for every admissible weight profile. Representative geometric, stretched-exponential, polynomial, and block-structured profiles illustrate all possible finite and infinite decay-threshold regimes.
